notes: Overview: NanoForge builds an IDE-integrated PR assistant used by internal engineering + a handful of early customers ("ForgeBot"). Focused on automated diff summarization, suggested review comments, and ranking/change-priority for engineers.

Why Redwood: need predictable low-latency streaming into VSCode Live Share sessions, model pinning per repo to avoid comment drift across releases, and private deployment options for regulated pilots.
Workload profile: average PR size ~120 LOC; expect 3-5 suggested inline comments per PR; peak concurrent reviewers ~40 across org; nightly batch re-run on open PRs for re-ranking ~2500 PRs/day.
Latency targets: interactive sessions need first-token streaming <120ms when connected to EU/NA regions; overall end-to-end PR analysis (cold) target <6s for 120 LOC diffs in Dedicated config.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market — willing to pay for Dedicated capacity but want Optimize recommendations to keep token/unit cost predictable. Interested in caching prefix outputs for repeated patterns.

Model preferences: prefer open/quantized variants they can pin (example request: gpt-neoX-20B-quant-v2 or redwood-compat-7B-fp16). Must support deterministic rollouts and rollback by commit hash or model-version label.
Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to smaller pinned model when Dedicated capacity limited; require fallback behavior to be configurable per repo/team (e.g., allow degraded ranking-only mode).

Security/compliance notes: enterprise customers require SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, audit logs for all inference calls, KMS integration for key material, retention controls for repo-specific prompt/response retention, and option for on-premises air-gapped package for certain regulated customers.

POC plan (current): 2-week sandbox on Redwood Dedicated with 2 nodes (A100-ish equivalent), run on 3 pilot repos (backend, infra, frontend). Measure latency distribution, cost per PR, and comment precision/recall vs. human reviewers. SE to gather eval prompts and golden-label PRs.
